text.brief: On September 29, 1964, Secretary of State Dean Rusk told the press that the People's Republic might explode its first nuclear device in the near future.
text.record: American intelligence had tracked the test site at Lop Nur and judged a test likely within months. The Party detonated its first device on October 16, 1964, two days after Nikita Khrushchev lost power in Moscow ([FRUS 1964-68, Vol. XXX: summary (the first Chinese nuclear explosion)](https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1964-68v30/summary); [Statement by the President on the First Chinese Nuclear Device (American Presidency Project)](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/statement-the-president-the-first-chinese-nuclear-device)). Lyndon Johnson's statement that day said the test came as no surprise to the government ([Statement by the President on the First Chinese Nuclear Device, October 16, 1964 (American Presidency Project, UC Santa Barbara)](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/statement-the-president-the-first-chinese-nuclear-device)).
text.reading: The defender decided before the event and spent the surprise in advance, so the test landed as a confirmed forecast rather than a shock. Pre-announcement is the Phase principle run against a psychological effect.
text.gapText: Data Architecture. The warning held because an owner mapped it to a public statement before the event.
text.fix: Pre-announce what intelligence judges likely when surprise is the adversary's aim, as the United States did again before Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
